business_scope.primary_industry_name: Tailoring of Licensed Theatrical Costume Robes and Synthetic Wigs

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - Federal statutory regime under the Canada Business Corporations Act; Common Law traditions prevail outside Quebec, Civil Law in Quebec
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), 2018
Canada-EU Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), 2017
Canada-China Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (FIPA), 2014
46 Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreements (FIPAs) and 90+ tax treaties in force; natural fit with Canada-US Tax Convention

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), SC 2000, c 17; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46; Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), RSC 1985, c C-44, sections 21.1-21.4 (Register of Individuals with Significant Control); Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001, SOR/2001-512; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 29; FINTRAC AML/CFT Rules; Bill C-42 mandatory beneficial-ownership filings to Corporations Canada; Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list; OFAC SDN list mandatory for USD payment rails
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access - corporation maintains an internal ISC register; mandatory disclosure to Corporations Canada, FINTRAC, CRA, and law enforcement; certain inspection rights for shareholders and creditors; full public beneficial-ownership registry phased and not yet fully operational

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport for each director, UBO, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or Commissioner of Oaths in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by Global Affairs Canada (for Canadian origin) or competent authority of country of issuance; Canadian consular legalization only where apostille unavailable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / corporate extract for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country corporate registry (e.g., Secretary of State, Companies House, MCA, CSB)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; subject to CRA permanent establishment review

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and six-month bank statement for each UBO (source of funds verification)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing financial institution of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized true copy plus apostille or consular legalization if required by receiving Canadian bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential and commercial address (utility bill or lease) for each director, UBO, and registered premises
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy by notary; apostille or consular legalization where foreign-issued

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and signatories against: (i) Global Affairs Canada Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List; (ii) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List for USD-denominated rails (Stripe / Shopify Payments); (iv) FINTRAC PEP determination under PCMLTFA section 9.1 with FATF-compliant enhanced due diligence; (v) CRA debarment and tax-registration integrity lists. High-risk PEP results require senior management sign-off, documented source-of-wealth, and 12-month refresh cycle; absent satisfactory evidence, appointment of the individual is refused.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada - Federal Corporation Online Filing Centre (www.corporationscanada.ic.gc.ca) with mandatory NUANS name search report
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Federal corporate names may be filed in English and/or French, or in bilingual format; mandatory legal element required: Limited, Ltee, Corporation, Corp., Incorporated, Inc.; name must be distinctive and not confusing with existing federal, provincial, or territorial names; NUANS report must accompany articles and is valid for 90 days; for Quebec extra-provincial registration, a French version is mandatory; transliteration into Latin script required for non-Roman characters.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection: (1) obtain a fresh NUANS report and refile with corrected distinctive element; (2) submit written reconsideration to the Director under CBCA section 10(6) within 30 days, attaching consent letters for sensitive tokens or corporate namesake; (3) if still refused, commence judicial review in the Federal Court within 30 days of the refusal under the Federal Courts Act; (4) interim alternative: register provincially (e.g., Ontario, BC) or adopt an assumed name via extra-provincial registration while definitive federal name adjudication proceeds.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Registered agent address and virtual office are acceptable only for service of process and corporate records; P.O. boxes are prohibited. A registered office must be maintained in the province of head office under CBCA section 19. Virtual office does not establish commercial substance for CRA tax-residence or GST/HST purposes; ISIC 3240 manufacturing operations require a physical production, warehousing, and retail/logistics premises with payroll and inventory substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate; approximately 7% probability (about 1 in 15) of unannounced CRA/GST audit visit, municipal fire/safety inspection, or provincial employment-standards inspection within the first 36 months; probability rises to 15-20% where large input tax credits, export duty drawbacks, or inter-provincial sourcing are claimed.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 6, 8, 9, 19, 28, 49, 106, 113.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (CBCA Form 1) filed via the Corporations Canada online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the CBCA. No escrow account is mandated. Incorporators may subscribe for one or more shares for nominal consideration, subject to the solvency requirements on share issuance.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the subscription for common shares subscribed by the incorporators is accepted, and such shares be issued upon receipt of consideration as fixed by the board; (2) the registered office of the Corporation in the province of registration is established at the address provided, and the corporate records and minute book be maintained at such address; (3) the persons named in the consent forms are appointed as directors and officers of the Corporation, with powers and duties prescribed by the bylaws and the Canada Business Corporations Act; and (4) any director or officer is authorized to execute additional filings, notices, and forms necessary to effect incorporation and initial registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation Name Search and NUANS Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada online name search portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a proposed corporate name through the NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) system, verify that the name includes a distinctive element and meets CBCA naming regulations, and optionally request a 90-day name reservation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused by the Director, file a revised name or appeal the refusal; an alternate name may be reserved promptly to avoid delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Authenticate Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete CBCA Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation), specifying share classes, restrictions on share transfer, registered office province, and initial directors. Incorporate the general bylaws by reference and execute the articles electronically or in writing.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director (Form 4, if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the articles are rejected, correct and resubmit the filing within the time indicated by Corporations Canada or request a Director's review under CBCA subsection 8(1).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Filing and Disburse Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the signed articles and consent forms, remit the prescribed filing fee via credit card or online payment, and confirm receipt through the electronic acknowledgment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment fails or the dossier is queried, reinstate the queue by correcting the discrepancy and paying the fee; Corporations Canada will issue a confirmation of filing date thereafter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue Certificate of Incorporation and Establish Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retrieve the Certificate of Incorporation in electronic PDF format, establish the corporate minute book containing bylaws, directors' register, shares register, and registered office designation, and issue share certificates to initial subscribers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a clerical error, apply to the Director for a corrected certificate under CBCA section 253.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with Revenue and Operational Agencies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the corporation's certificate and banking details, register for a CRA Business Number (BN), GST/HST account, corporate income tax account, payroll deductions (if employees will be hired), and any provincial import/export or sector registrations that may apply.
required_dossiers: Proposed date of first GST/HST reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, call the CRA business inquiry line to expedite the process; submit a conformed copy of the articles and explain the commercial urgency.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable under federal incorporation; provincial/territorial manufacturing regulators and municipal zoning or business licensing authorities may require permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Commercial / Manufacturing Licence (if applicable); not a federal statutory licence.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) / provincial environmental regulator (e.g., Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Typically registration-level or exempt for costume and wig production; a full EIA report is not required unless manufacturing processes emit substances subject to CEPA 1999 or provincial air and waste regulations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must meet provincial sewer by-law and environmental quality standards; VOC emissions from adhesives, paints, or synthetic fiber processing must comply with National Emission Control Benchmarks; waste handling must follow provincial waste and hazardous materials regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required under the applicable National Fire Code and municipal fire by-law; structural load approval is needed for any retail or manufacturing premises; workplace clearance must be obtained under provincial occupational health and safety acts (e.g., OHSA).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Federal Tax Authority and Portal
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities obtain statutory TIN (Business Number) and VAT ID by registering with CRA via My Business portal or Form RC1, submitting incorporation or business setup documents and proof of address.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available; corporations are taxed at entity level. No hybrid mismatch elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual taxable supplies for GST/HST registration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Registrants must file GST/HST returns electronically through the CRA My Business portal. Real-time fiscal clearance not mandated; digital stamping via approved software for certain transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada are zero-rated for GST/HST purposes. Offshore services may qualify under specific export rules.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits may lead to penalties of 50% or more of evaded tax, interest, and clawback of zero-rated amounts with potential criminal sanctions for fraudulent claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), in coordination with OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions) as the prudential banking supervisor and FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada) as the AML/CTF financial intelligence unit.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a fully liberalized floating-currency regime governed by the Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52) and the Bank Act (S.C. 1991, c. 46). The Canadian dollar (CAD) is freely convertible on both current-account (export/import of goods and services, royalties, management fees) and capital-account (FDI, portfolio investment, intercompany loans, dividends) at market-determined rates. Profit remittances by a federal CBCA corporation to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted and require no central bank approval, subject only to: (i) Part XIII Income Tax Act gross withholding on dividends (statutory 25%, treaty-reduced to 5%-15% for residents of treaty partners such as the US and UK); (ii) receipt of FX by a Canadian chartered bank is subject to a FINTRAC Electronic Funds Transfer Report (EFTR) where the remittance exceeds CAD 10,000; (iii) solvency of the corporation at the time of any reduction of capital under CBCA s.42. No exchange rationing, forced conversion, or investment approval applies to routine treasury transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender, no mandatory repatriation window, and no minimum conversion ratio under the Currency Act, Income Tax Act, or PCMLTFA. Export receipts denominated in USD or other foreign currencies may be retained indefinitely in a Canadian chartered-bank foreign-currency account (e.g., RBC USD Advantage account, TD Borderless Plan), held in an offshore USD account, used directly to settle foreign supplier invoices (fabric, wigs, props hardware), or converted to CAD at spot. Legal limits are limited to standard FINTRAC record-keeping thresholds (CAD 10,000 per transaction), the CBCA requirement for directors to maintain adequate financial records, and CRA transfer-pricing and functional-currency reporting obligations where the functional-currency election is made.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account: not statutorily required under the CBCA; use a segregated 'Trust/Subscription Account' held by corporate counsel for pre-issuance capital, then convert to an Operational CAD Account plus a USD-denominated foreign-currency sub-account.
Operational CAD Account with USD Borderless Plan sub-account and cross-border wire sweep to TD Bank, N.A. (US affiliate).
Operational CAD/USD Account; optional contractual escrow through BMO Escrow Services for importer-supplier deposits.
Operational Account with CIBC 'Cross Border' USD account linked to CIBC US; no statutory escrow applies to corporate capital.
Operational Global Transfer Account in CAD/USD/MXN; structured trade desk for documentary letters of credit.
Operational CAD Account with USD omnibus clearing; niche strength in Quebec manufacturing supply chains.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: HIGH as a supplemental payment and FX-conversion rail; LOW as a primary treasury bank. Wise Business, Payoneer, and Stripe Treasury (embedded in Shopify Payments) operate in Canada as payment service providers or through authorized bank partners under the Retail Payment Activities Act (S.C. 2021, c. 23, s. 150) framework; they offer multi-currency balances, virtual USD/EUR/GBP accounts, and low-cost FX conversion suited to cosplay e-commerce collections. Legal constraints: (i) EMIs are not Schedule I/II chartered banks under the Bank Act and do not hold CDIC deposit insurance; (ii) they lack direct LYNX/ACSS access, so they cannot provide same-day CAD clearing, high-value wire finality, or trade-finance instruments such as letters of credit; (iii) RPAA registration with the Bank of Canada is mandatory for retail payment activities and must be verified during onboarding; (iv) concentration risk: retain no more than 30%-50% of treasury liquidity at any EMI and sweep balances daily to the Schedule I bank to avoid safeguarding-status disputes and PSP insolvency losses.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statute mandates physical appearance or an in-branch KYC interview; FINTRAC's client-identification rules (PCMLTFA s.11 and associated regulations) permit non-face-to-face verification. In practice, Tier 1 banks apply a hybrid model: at least one director or authorized officer must complete a FINTRAC-compliant video identity verification (e.g., RBC Video ID, TD Virtual Interview), and the corporate package must include certified copies of the Certificate of Incorporation, CBCA Articles, and a registered-office attestation. For corporations with a majority non-resident directorship, most banks (TD, Scotiabank, NBC) condition fast-track onboarding on a single in-person meeting at a Toronto, Vancouver, Calgary, or Montreal business-banking center, or accept a notarized identity package couriered from the home country. Remote-only onboarding is routinely available for wholly Canadian-resident beneficial owners; mixed or foreign-UBO structures add enhanced due diligence, a two-to-four-week processing timeline, and an internal compliance referral.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: nominee directors, a multi-tier foreign holding chain (e.g., a holding company in a low-tax jurisdiction), or non-disclosure of 25%+ beneficial ownership under FINTRAC beneficial-ownership rules (PCMLTFA s.9.3 and s.9.4).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (i) a fully populated CBCA securities register and notarized shareholder register; (ii) a signed and dated Beneficial Ownership Attestation identifying the ultimate individual owners, whether Canadian or non-resident; (iii) a corporate organizational chart covering every intermediate entity, with certificates of good standing or active status for each; (iv) a board resolution appointing banking signatories and certifying the corporate structure; (v) government-issued photo ID, proof of residential address dated within six months, and, where applicable, a CRA letter confirming the T2 corporate tax account or the Corporations Canada filing receipt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk source of founding capital: a capital injection from a jurisdiction on the FATF grey-list, a high-risk tax haven, or a remittance exceeding CAD 50,000 sourced from cryptocurrency exchange balances.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide six months of bank statements from the remitting shareholder account evidencing legitimate funds accumulation; a source-of-wealth narrative (business sale agreement, employment payslips, inheritance documents); tax clearance documentation (CRA Notice of Assessment or the equivalent foreign tax return); and for crypto-derived funds, a transaction-ledger export from the exchange plus a commercial blockchain-forensic report (Chainalysis or Elliptic) confirming wallet provenance and the absence of sanctioned-source tags.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce refund and chargeback anomaly: custom-cosplay manufacturing with frequent card-not-present chargebacks on Shopify Payments or Stripe, a refund-to-revenue ratio approaching or exceeding 1%, or performance obligations exceeding 180 days.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a business plan with a product catalog and pricing model; 12 months of Shopify Payments or Stripe settlement history and dispute logs (target chargeback ratio below 0.75%); the merchant-processing agreement and published refund and returns policy; production evidence including fabric and wig supplier purchase orders, CBSA customs declarations (B3/e-manifest), and freight-forwarder bills of lading; order-level customer records demonstrating delivery milestones; a PIPEDA and privacy compliance binder; and an independent accountant's cash-flow projection showing that customer prepayments are recorded as deferred revenue rather than financing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party and offshore 'matching' payment pattern: split disbursements to suppliers in Guangdong fabric mills, Zhejiang wig manufacturers, and US prop hardware vendors from a newly opened account, with obligor or beneficiary name mismatch or payments made to third-party collection accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce executed master supply agreements with each named supplier; commercial invoice and packing-list sets; CBSA import-entry summaries; SWIFT MT103 payment instructions that recite the underlying purchase-order number and commercial invoice number; bank-confirmed supplier-beneficiary account attestation whenever payment is made to an entity different from the nominal supplier, with the corporate relationship certified; and a supplier-reconciliation ledger audited quarterly by the corporation's CPA.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant rail: the non-resident shareholder wires via SWIFT MT103 to the corporation's operating account at RBC, TD, or BMO; the wire instruction must state the purpose as 'CAP - Capital subscription to CA_CORP' or 'LOAN - Intercompany shareholder loan', cite the CBCA certificate number, and clear through LYNX/ACSS upon receipt. Threshold alerts: any inbound wire exceeding CAD 10,000 generates a FINTRAC EFTR filed by the receiving bank, which may pause funds under 'reasonable measures' to verify the subscription. Pre-delivered documentation must include the board resolution authorizing share issuance or borrowing, the executed subscription agreement, the issued share certificate, and, for shareholder loans, an arm's-length interest-bearing loan note satisfying Part XIII withholding documentation and CRA thin-capitalization compliance (debt-to-equity 1.5:1) where the lender is a 25%+ non-resident shareholder. Investment Canada Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. 28 (1st Supp.)): the establishment of a new Canadian business by a WTO-member investor is exempt from review where asset value is below the annual threshold (2024: CAD 5.34 billion in enterprise value); only a post-incorporation notification is required, and no pre-transaction capital escrow is mandated.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 (telegraphic transfer) for direct supplier settlements on invoices below CAD 100,000 from fabric and hardware vendors; USD payments settle via the Canadian bank's US correspondent (RBC BNY Mellon, TD CTX/SWA) and CNY/INR/EUR via domestic correspondents; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (sight or 30-60-90 day usance) issued through RBC, TD, or BMO trade finance via SWIFT MT700 for bulk purchases (latex moulds, silk supplies) above CAD 100,000 or when a supplier mandates LC terms; (iii) documentary collections (D/P, D/A) as a cost-reduced alternative in established supplier relationships; (iv) domestic CAD disbursements via ACSS (same-day low-value clearing) and the Real-Time Rail (RTR) for Canadian freight forwarding, CBSA duty payments, and warehouse charges. All outward wires exceeding CAD 10,000 are EFTR-reported by the bank; FX conversions are executed at the bank's intraday spot plus a typical 40-60 basis point spread, mitigable by maintaining a USD settlement sub-account and invoicing suppliers in their local currency.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD spot outright and deliverable forward contracts (typically requiring 10%-25% margin or collateral), documented under the Canadian Bankers Association master agreement or an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement; no Bank of Canada authorization is required.

Foreign-exchange swaps (rollover structures) matching USD revenue receipts against CAD operating expenditures; permitted without restriction but requiring a board-approved derivatives policy and an annual risk attestation to the bank under OSFI Guideline E-4.

Cross-currency base swaps (USD/CAD) converting floating-rate USD shareholder-loan interest into fixed-rate CAD-equivalent liabilities; permissible for long-term hedging underlying the intercompany capital structure.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on offshore CNY (CNH) and INR; admissible strictly for hedging the underlying cosplay-apparel supply chain (fabric and wig import payables), with banks booking these only where genuine commercial exposure is demonstrated; NDF spreads are typically 60-120 basis points over deliverable forwards.

Vanilla FX options (CAD put / USD call) remain legally permissible in Canada but are operationally available only where the corporation executes an ISDA and adopts a Qualified Business Derivatives User policy; for a Low_Risk_Standard cosplay manufacturer, direct forwards plus natural offset through multi-currency accounts constitutes the recommended minimum-viable hedging configuration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation; if a prior annual return was filed within the preceding 12 months, within 60 days after the anniversary date of that prior filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of CAD 25 for overdue returns; summary conviction fine up to CAD 5,000 under s.263(3); administrative strike-off by the Director pursuant to s.212 CBCA after one year of continuous non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Meeting and shareholder approval of financial statements (CBCA ss.133 and 155)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders (internal corporate record; no regulator filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First meeting within 18 months of incorporation and thereafter within 15 months of the prior meeting; financial statements must be presented at each meeting within the same window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors are liable to summary conviction for failure to call the meeting; Corporations Canada may administratively dissolve the corporation under s.212 CBCA for persistent non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Notice of change of directors or registered office (CBCA ss.106 and 113) - event-driven recurrence in an operating cosplay apparel manufacturer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days of any director appointment, resignation, or registered office address change occurring during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under CBCA s.106(5) and s.113(4) carrying summary conviction penalties; stale registry data can block extra-provincial licences, bank financing, and third-party contracting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register annual refresh (CBCA ss.21.1 to 21.3)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal statutory register; production on demand to the Director of Corporations Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Reasonable steps to identify significant-control individuals at least once each fiscal year; register updates within 15 days of any share transfer or change in control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Summary conviction fine up to CAD 5,000; directors and shareholders may face liability for knowingly failing to report significant control or permitting false register entries

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Extra-provincial registration renewals for each province where physical operations occur
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial corporate registries (e.g., Ontario Companies Office, Corporate Registry BC, Registraire des entreprises Quebec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based under each province's Business Corporations Act; typically 30 to 60 days following the federal anniversary date or fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of local authority to carry on business; late penalties, interest, and administrative cancellation of extra-provincial registration; amounts vary by province

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under CBCA s.171, appointment of an independent auditor is mandatory unless the corporation is not a reporting issuer or distributing corporation, its gross annual revenues for the most recently completed financial year were CAD 1,000,000 or less, and all shareholders unanimously consent to waive the audit; otherwise a licensed CPA auditor must be appointed at each annual meeting
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (Part I of the CPA Canada Handbook) or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, Part II); a private non-distributing cosplay apparel manufacturer is permitted to elect ASPE; financial statements must be prepared in accordance with Canadian GAAP and presented at each annual meeting under s.155 CBCA

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under CBCA ss.21.1 to 21.3, the corporation must take reasonable steps at least once each fiscal year to identify every individual with significant control, defined as holding 25% or more of voting shares or holding de facto control; the ISC register must be updated within 15 days of any share transfer or change in control; no public annual filing of the register is made with Corporations Canada, but the register must be maintained on-site and delivered to the Director upon request
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control
Minute Book (articles, by-laws, resolutions, meeting minutes)
Accounting records supporting the annual financial statements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 300-1,500 (USD 220-1,100) per year for registered office and corporate agent services retained for the federal jurisdiction

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The federal general corporate rate is 15% after the 10% provincial abatement and the 13% general rate reduction applied to the 38% basic Part I rate. A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) may access the Small Business Deduction, yielding a 9% federal effective rate on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income; the deduction is statutorily unavailable to non-resident-controlled corporations under ITA s. 125(6). Preferential deductions available to a costume and cosplay prop apparel manufacturer include the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit (35% refundable for a qualifying CCPC on eligible Canadian expenditures up to the CAD 3,000,000 expenditure limit; 15% non-refundable for non-CCPCs), accelerated capital cost allowance under CCA Class 53 at 50% declining balance for qualifying manufacturing and processing machinery and equipment, and the elective deferral or reserve mechanisms for amounts not receivable until a subsequent year. No discretionary federal tax holiday exists for this IP-sensitive light manufacturing activity.
